To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the performance of the feature-selection methods is strongly related to the distribution model, (2) the performance is also strongly related to the sample size, and (3) the performance is related to the relation between the features.

(1) filter methods have better or similar performances with wrapper methods for hard problems, (2) wrapper methods have better performance with large samples, (3) ReliefF has worse performance than t-test for most cases, and (4) ReliefF-based wrapper method shows performance similar to t-test-based wrapper methods.
the performance of feature selection depends on the number of features, the number of useful features, and the relations between features.
